Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Ghana Bauxite Company commits to opening Awaso to commercial activity Source : Nana Yaw Gyimah 23 November 2026 9:21pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Ghana Bauxite Company Limited says it is deliberately using its expanding operations at Awaso to open the catchment communities to wider commercial activity.
After the mine's takeover by the IOP Group, investments are being made to improve its operations and expand job opportunities.
According to the General Manager, Alexander Gyedu, the group targets enhancing the local economies of the mine's catchment area through industrialisation.
"It is the story of how an established industrial operation can become a catalyst around which other businesses, services, skills, and investments begin to grow," he said.
Mr. Gyedu emphasised: "When an enterprise grows, the true measure of its impact is not only what happens inside its gates. It is what begins to happen around those gates."
He was speaking at the opening of the Ecobank Awaso Branch, which comes after the signing of a $250-million funding agreement with Ecobank Ghana to finance the company's expansion drive.
GBC has in recent years been investing in mining operations, equipment, logistics, and operating capability, moving away from traditional drill-and-blast methods towards more modern mining techniques.
That expansion is also connected to Ghana's National Integrated Aluminium Industry Programme, which identifies the expansion of the Awaso mine and the development of an alumina refinery as critical to the country's aluminium industry strategy.
GBC argued the growth being realised is expected to drive local economies in the catchment communities.
The company's partnership with Ecobank has resulted in the opening of the bank's new branch at Awaso, which is expected to improve banking services for residents.
Speaking at the opening of the new branch, the Executive Director of Corporate and Investment Banking for Ghana and Anglophone West Africa for Ecobank, Henry Ampong, revealed the bank's decision to establish a presence in the community was part of a broader commitment to making banking services accessible to people in emerging economies.
He emphasised commitment to supporting small and medium-sized enterprises, and to advancing women-led and women-owned businesses.
Meanwhile, Western North Regional Minister, Wilbert Petty Brentum, also linked the bank's opening to Awaso's strategic location and the government's infrastructure agenda for the Western North Region.
He said many roads in the region are receiving a facelift to enhance business.
He also said discussions are ongoing to bring back the railway from Awaso to Takoradi, and pointed to interest expressed at a recent investment summit in Accra in supporting railway infrastructure and in putting up a bigger agricultural warehouse in Awaso, from which farm produce from the hinterlands could be brought to Awaso and transported by rail to Takoradi and other places.
"Setting up a bank here in Awaso is very strategic," the Regional Minister said, urging residents to open accounts with Ecobank to make its presence in Awaso sustainable and to encourage expansion to other areas.
The relationship between the two institutions goes beyond the branch. On 28th October 2026, GBC appointed Ecobank Ghana as exclusive mandated arranger for proposed financing facilities of up to US$250,000,000 to support the next phase of GBC's mine expansion, including capital investment and working capital requirements.
GBC stressed that the branch opening and the financing transaction are distinct matters, but said together they demonstrate how economic ecosystems develop.
"Investment attracts services. Services enable enterprise. Enterprise creates opportunity. And opportunity, when it is responsibly managed, becomes development," Mr. Gyedu said.
That multiplier effect, GBC said, is what it wants to see around the mine - local entrepreneurs graduating from small informal transactions into properly managed enterprises, and young people seeing that an industrial economy creates careers, not only for miners, but for accountants, bankers, technicians, engineers, geologists, IT specialists, environmental specialists, and business owners.
GBC has established a dedicated Community Relations Office in Awaso to create a more structured channel for engaging surrounding communities, including local enterprises, initiatives, and community programmes.
